chapter: Chicago pioneers, community and New Orleans brotherhood
title: Erskine Tate's and Sammy Stewart's bands
summary: Saunders describes Tate's Vendome Theatre band and Sammy Stewart's immaculate band at the Metropolitan around 1928-30.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Let's talk about some of the people that you knew and played with through the years.
You were talking about Erskine Tate.

Yeah, well, I talked about Erskine -- I never -- see, he was a little before my time. He started in the '20s, he was in the '20s, and he had that great band at the Vendome Theatre. And it was just a rare treat to go -- the people used to go, not for the movie, not for whatever, they went to hear that band.

And in the band, he had greats like Earl Hines and at one time, Teddy Weatherford on piano. He featured all these people -- Louis Armstrong and Jimmy Bertran and Bud Scott worked there, all these different people.

And then I remember, another great band was -- in later years, well, around '28, around in there, '29,'30, Sammy Stewart. He had a terrific band, and very clean and dressed in their tuxedos and everything. And they looked like they just stepped out of a bandbox. And then they started naming places bandboxes, and this is where -- they'd say he just stepped out of a bandbox.

And he had a tremendous band there at the Metropolitan Theatre, here, and then he had worked at the Sunset and some of those nightclubs before that, too. And he had a terrific band.
Well, did he just conduct -- well, Tate just conducted then.
Yeah. Tate was a violinist, but he just conducted.
Well, was Sammy Stewart the same type --
